note.question: How should a firm coordinate resistance to activist pressure and lobbying over a policy life cycle whose public opinion is slowed by political polarization?
note.overview: An activist strategically chooses campaign effort while a firm chooses a resistance threshold and, once legislation becomes feasible, lobbying. The infinite-horizon game is explicitly solved under pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibrium as polarized public beliefs evolve.

source.section: Two-Phase Model of the Policy Life Cycle
source.quote: In the early phase of the cycle, public support is too weak to enable the passage of legislation, but mobilization by social movement groups occurs and may be sufficient to induce firms to adopt new practices voluntarily.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In every period the activist chooses effort before campaign harm is realized. After observing harm, the firm concedes or resists. Once majority beliefs cross the legislative threshold, a resisting firm can also lobby to block a bill; if lobbying fails and a bill arrives, adoption is mandated. Otherwise the game proceeds with updated public beliefs.
